literal: On the chia-hsü day of the twelfth month, Li Hsiu-chih, Staff Officer of the Right Army, was made Governor of Chiao Province.
idiomatic: On the chia-hsü day of the twelfth month, Li Hsiu-chih, Staff Officer of the Right Army, was appointed Governor of Chiao Province.

literal: On the keng-yin day, the fifth imperial son Shao was established as Prince of Lu-ling, and Lang, son of Prince of Chiang-hsia I-chung, as Prince of Nan-feng County.
idiomatic: On the keng-yin day, the fifth imperial son Shao was created Prince of Lu-ling, and Lang, son of Prince of Chiang-hsia I-chung, was created Prince of Nan-feng County.

literal: In the first month of spring of the tenth year, on the chia-yin day, Prince of Ching-ling I-hsuan was changed in enfeoffment to Prince of Nan-ch'iao.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the tenth year, on the chia-yin day, Prince of Ching-ling I-hsuan was redesignated Prince of Nan-ch'iao.

literal: Wang Chung-te, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü Province, was additionally made Governor of Yen Province; Tuan Hung, Administrator of Huai-nan, was made Governor of Ch'ing Province.
idiomatic: Wang Chung-te, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü Province, was additionally appointed Governor of Yen Province; Tuan Hung, Administrator of Huai-nan, became Governor of Ch'ing Province.

literal: On the chi-wei day, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the chi-wei day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: The elderly living alone and those afflicted with the six infirmities who could not support themselves were each granted five hu of grain.
idiomatic: The elderly living alone and those afflicted with the six infirmities who could not support themselves each received five hu of grain.

literal: I-hsin, Prince of Ch'ang-sha and General of the Rear and Governor of Yü Province, was advanced in title to General of the Army.
idiomatic: Prince of Ch'ang-sha I-hsin, General of the Rear and Governor of Yü Province, was advanced to General of the Army.

literal: On the wu-hsü day of the fourth month in summer, Tuan Hung, Governor of Ch'ing Province, was additionally made Governor of Chi Province.
idiomatic: On the wu-hsü day of the fourth month in summer, Tuan Hung, Governor of Ch'ing Province, was additionally appointed Governor of Chi Province.

literal: Hsiao Szu-hua, Marquis of Feng-yang, was made Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces.
idiomatic: Hsiao Szu-hua, Marquis of Feng-yang, was appointed Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces.

literal: In the fifth month, the King of Lin-yi sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, the King of Lin-yi sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the i-hai day of the sixth month, Wei Lang, former Governor of Ch'ing Province, was made Governor of Kuang Province.
idiomatic: On the i-hai day of the sixth month, Wei Lang, former Governor of Ch'ing Province, was appointed Governor of Kuang Province.

literal: The state of Ho-lo-tan in Ch'an-p'o sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: The state of Ho-lo-tan in Ch'an-p'o sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the wu-hsü day of the seventh month in autumn, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Yi, Liang, and Ch'in provinces.
idiomatic: On the wu-hsü day of the seventh month in autumn, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Yi, Liang, and Ch'in provinces.

literal: The commanderies of Sung-ning and Sung-hsing were established in Yi Province.
idiomatic: The commanderies of Sung-ning and Sung-hsing were established in Yi Province.

literal: On the ting-ch'ou day of the eighth month, T'ai-yüan Commandery was established in Ch'ing Province.
idiomatic: On the ting-ch'ou day of the eighth month, T'ai-yüan Commandery was established in Ch'ing Province.

literal: On the hsin-ssu day, Tao Yen-chih, General Who Protects the Army, died.
idiomatic: On the hsin-ssu day, Tao Yen-chih, General Who Protects the Army, died.

literal: In the eleventh month of winter, the Ti chieftain Yang Nan-t'ang raided Han-ch'uan.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, the Di chieftain Yang Nan-t'ang raided Han-ch'uan.

literal: On the ting-wei day, Chen Fa-hu, Governor of Liang Province, abandoned the city and fled; Nan-t'ang seized Liang Province.
idiomatic: On the ting-wei day, Chen Fa-hu, Governor of Liang Province, abandoned the city and fled, and Nan-t'ang took possession of Liang Province.

literal: In the first month of spring of the eleventh year, the outlaw Ma Ta-hsüan and his band of several hundred men raided T'ai-shan; [13] the province and commanderies suppressed and pacified them.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the eleventh year, the outlaw Ma Ta-hsüan and his band of several hundred men raided T'ai-shan; [13] the province and commanderies suppressed them.

literal: On the kuei-yu day of the second month, Li Tan-chih, Administrator of Chiao-chih, was made Governor of Chiao Province.
idiomatic: On the kuei-yu day of the second month, Li Tan-chih, Administrator of Chiao-chih, was appointed Governor of Chiao Province.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, Hsiao Szu-hua, Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces, defeated the Ti chieftain Yang Nan-t'ang, and Liang Province was pacified.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Hsiao Szu-hua, Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces, defeated the Di chieftain Yang Nan-t'ang, and Liang Province was pacified.

literal: On the ting-mao day of the fifth month, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for the region north of Chien-ko in Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces.
idiomatic: On the ting-mao day of the fifth month, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for the region north of Chien-ko in Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces.

literal: On the wu-yin day, Chu-chü Mao-ch'ien was made Grand General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: On the wu-yin day, Chu-chü Mao-ch'ien was appointed Grand General Who Campaigns West and Governor of Liang Province.

literal: That month, the capital suffered great flooding.
idiomatic: That month, the capital suffered severe flooding.

literal: On the ting-wei day of the sixth month, Wei Commandery was abolished.
idiomatic: On the ting-wei day of the sixth month, Wei Commandery was abolished.

literal: That year, Lin-yi, Fu-nan, and Ho-lo-tan sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: That year, Lin-yi, Fu-nan, and Ho-lo-tan sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the hsin-yu day of the first month in spring of the twelfth year, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the hsin-yu day of the first month in spring of the twelfth year, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: On the hsin-wei day, the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.
idiomatic: On the hsin-wei day, the Emperor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.

literal: On the kuei-yu day, Feng Hung, ruler of the Yellow Dragon state, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yen.
idiomatic: On the kuei-yu day, Feng Hung, ruler of the Yellow Dragon state, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yen.

literal: On the i-yu day of the fourth month in summer, [14] Yin Ching-jen, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was additionally made General of the Central Army.
idiomatic: On the i-yu day of the fourth month in summer, [14] Yin Ching-jen, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was additionally appointed General of the Central Army.

literal: On the ping-ch'en day, an edict said: "The house of Chou attained tranquillity through its many officers; the rise of the Han house likewise relied on obtaining men.
idiomatic: On the ping-ch'en day, an edict said: "The Zhou house attained peace through its many officers; the Han dynasty's rise likewise depended on finding the right men.

literal: I have dreamed and waked delighting in the worthy, and this has been so for many days, yet sagely discernment is hard to attain and bright promotion has had no effect.
idiomatic: I have long dreamed and waked with joy in worthy men, yet sage discernment remains hard to reach and bright promotion has borne no fruit.

literal: Thus outstanding talent remains in the wilds and the storerooms stand empty at court; eternally recalling former records, my shame in virtue runs deep.
idiomatic: Outstanding talent still wanders beyond office, and the court's storerooms stand empty; thinking forever on the records of old, I am deeply ashamed of my own virtue.

literal: To raise those whom you know is Confucius's earnest instruction; presenting scholars and assigning office is the established norm of former ages.
idiomatic: To recommend those you know is Confucius's earnest teaching; presenting scholars and appointing them to office is the settled standard of former ages.

literal: Let an edict be proclaimed within and without, each making recommendations.
idiomatic: Let an edict now be proclaimed within and without, and let each office make recommendations.

literal: They shall be selected and promoted according to measure, to observe their employ."
idiomatic: They shall be weighed and advanced by their measure, that we may see what use they can serve."

literal: That night, the capital suffered an earthquake.
idiomatic: That night, the capital was struck by an earthquake.

literal: In the sixth month, Tan-yang, Huai-nan, Wu-hsing, and I-hsing suffered great flooding; in the capital people traveled by boat.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, Tan-yang, Huai-nan, Wu-hsing, and I-hsing suffered severe flooding, and in the capital people went about by boat.

literal: On the chi-yu day, several million hu of grain from Hsü, Yü, and Southern Yen provinces and from the commanderies of K'uai-chi and Hsüan-ch'eng were granted to the people of the five commanderies who had suffered flooding.
idiomatic: On the chi-yu day, several million hu of grain from Hsü, Yü, and Southern Yen provinces and from K'uai-chi and Hsüan-ch'eng commanderies were distributed to the people of the five flood-stricken commanderies.

literal: That month, the sale of wine was prohibited.
idiomatic: That month, the sale of wine was prohibited.

literal: The Lion Country sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: The Lion Country sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the hsin-yu day of the seventh month in autumn, [15] the states of Ch'an-p'o-sa-ta and Fu-nan both sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: On the hsin-yu day of the seventh month in autumn, [15] the states of Ch'an-p'o-sa-ta and Fu-nan both sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the jen-shên day of the eighth month, the three commanderies of Southern Chin-shou, Southern Hsin-pa, and Northern Pa-hsi were established in Yi Province.
idiomatic: On the jen-shên day of the eighth month, the three commanderies of Southern Chin-shou, Southern Hsin-pa, and Northern Pa-hsi were established in Yi Province.

literal: [16] On the i-hai day, all overdue obligations in the flood-stricken commanderies were remitted.
idiomatic: [16] On the i-hai day, all overdue obligations in the flood-stricken commanderies were remitted.

literal: In the ninth month, the bandit Chang Hsün of Shu Commandery rose in rebellion.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, the bandit Chang Hsün of Shu Commandery rose in rebellion.

literal: In the eleventh month of winter, Ch'ü Tao-fu, Acting Staff Officer of the Right Army, was made Governor of Chiao Province.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Ch'ü Tao-fu, Acting Staff Officer of the Right Army, was appointed Governor of Chiao Province.

literal: On the kuei-ch'ou day of the first month in spring of the thirteenth year, the Emperor was ill and did not hold court audience.
idiomatic: On the kuei-ch'ou day of the first month in spring of the thirteenth year, the Emperor was ill and did not hold court audience.

literal: On the chi-wei day of the third month, Tan Tao-chi, Minister of Works and Governor of Chiang Province, was guilty and executed.
idiomatic: On the chi-wei day of the third month, Tan Tao-chi, Minister of Works and Governor of Chiang Province, was found guilty and executed.

literal: On the keng-shên day, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the keng-shên day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: I-hsuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao and General of the Central Army, was made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Chiang Province.
idiomatic: Prince of Nan-ch'iao I-hsuan, General of the Central Army, was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Chiang Province.

literal: On the wu-ch'en day of the fifth month in summer, Wang Chung-te, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was advanced in title to Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: On the wu-ch'en day of the fifth month in summer, Wang Chung-te, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was advanced to Grand General Who Pacifies the North.

literal: On the keng-ch'en day, Wang Fang-p'ai, Staff Officer of the General Who Campaigns North, was made Governor of Yen Province.
idiomatic: On the keng-ch'en day, Wang Fang-p'ai, Staff Officer of the General Who Campaigns North, was appointed Governor of Yen Province.

literal: In the sixth month, Kao-li and the Prince of Wu-tu sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, Kao-li and the Prince of Wu-tu sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the keng-yin day of the eighth month, Yin Ching-jen, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Central Army, was changed to General Who Protects the Army.
idiomatic: On the keng-yin day of the eighth month, Yin Ching-jen, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Central Army, was redesignated General Who Protects the Army.

literal: On the kuei-ch'ou day of the ninth month, the second imperial son Chün was established as Prince of Shih-hsing, and the third imperial son Chün was established as Prince of Wu-ling.
idiomatic: On the kuei-ch'ou day of the ninth month, the second imperial son Chün was created Prince of Shih-hsing, and the third imperial son Chün was created Prince of Wu-ling.

literal: On the hsin-mao day of the first month in spring of the fourteenth year, the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the hsin-mao day of the first month in spring of the fourteenth year, the Emperor personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: Civil and military officials were granted one rank of promotion;
idiomatic: Civil and military officials were promoted one rank;

literal: the elderly living alone and those afflicted with the six infirmities who could not support themselves were each granted five hu of grain.
idiomatic: the elderly living alone and those afflicted with the six infirmities who could not support themselves each received five hu of grain.

literal: On the jen-tzu day of the second month, Liu Chen-tao, Colonel of Footsoldiers, was made Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces.
idiomatic: On the jen-tzu day of the second month, Liu Chen-tao, Colonel of Footsoldiers, was appointed Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces.

literal: [17] Editorial note seventeen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
idiomatic: [17] Editorial note seventeen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

literal: On the ting-wei day of the fourth month in summer, Chou Chi-chih, General Who Assists the State, was made Governor of Yi Province.
idiomatic: On the ting-wei day of the fourth month in summer, Chou Chi-chih, General Who Assists the State, was appointed Governor of Yi Province.

literal: On the wu-wu day of the eighth month in autumn, Hsu Sen-chih, Gentleman of the Gold Section in the Masters of Writing, was made Governor of Chiao Province.
idiomatic: On the wu-wu day of the eighth month in autumn, Hsu Sen-chih, Gentleman of the Gold Section in the Masters of Writing, was appointed Governor of Chiao Province.

literal: On the hsin-yu day of the twelfth month in winter, the rite of congratulating on snow was suspended.
idiomatic: On the hsin-yu day of the twelfth month in winter, the rite of congratulating on snow was suspended.

literal: The states of Ho-nan, the Prince of the Western River, and Ho-lo-tan all sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: The states of Ho-nan, the Prince of the Western River, and Ho-lo-tan all sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: [18] Editorial note eighteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
idiomatic: [18] Editorial note eighteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

literal: On the ting-wei day of the second month in spring of the fifteenth year, Murong Yen of T'o-yü-hun, General Who Pacifies the East, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Ch'in and Ho provinces.
idiomatic: On the ting-wei day of the second month in spring of the fifteenth year, Murong Yen of T'o-yü-hun, General Who Pacifies the East, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Ch'in and Ho provinces.

literal: On the chia-ch'en day of the fourth month in summer, Prince of Yen Hung sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: On the chia-ch'en day of the fourth month in summer, Prince of Yen Hung sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: [19] The consort of the Heir Apparent, of the Yin clan, was established, and the kings, dukes, and those below were each granted gifts according to rank.
idiomatic: [19] The consort of the Heir Apparent of the Yin clan was installed, and kings, dukes, and officials below them were each granted gifts according to rank.

literal: On the chi-ssu day, Chen, King of Wa, was made General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: On the chi-ssu day, Chen, King of Wa, was appointed General Who Pacifies the East.

literal: On the chi-ch'ou day, Yin Mu, Special Grandee and Right Grandee of Splendid Virtue, died.
idiomatic: On the chi-ch'ou day, Yin Mu, Special Grandee and Right Grandee of Splendid Virtue, died.

literal: On the hsin-mao day, Wang Chung-te, Grand General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü Province, died.
idiomatic: On the hsin-mao day, Wang Chung-te, Grand General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü Province, died.

literal: On the jen-ch'en day, Liu Tsun-k'ao, General of the Right Guards, was made Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces.
idiomatic: On the jen-ch'en day, Liu Tsun-k'ao, General of the Right Guards, was appointed Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces.

literal: On the hsin-wei day of the seventh month in autumn, there was an earthquake.
idiomatic: On the hsin-wei day of the seventh month in autumn, there was an earthquake.

literal: On the chia-hsü day, Hsu Hsün, Administrator of Ch'en and Nan-tun, was made Governor of Ning Province.
idiomatic: On the chia-hsü day, Hsu Hsün, Administrator of Ch'en and Nan-tun, was appointed Governor of Ning Province.

literal: On the hsin-ch'ou day of the eighth month, Chao Po-fu, General of the Left Guards, was made Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces.
idiomatic: On the hsin-ch'ou day of the eighth month, Chao Po-fu, General of the Left Guards, was appointed Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces.

literal: On the chia-yin day, Lu Hui, Administrator of Shih-hsing, was made Governor of Kuang Province.
idiomatic: On the chia-yin day, Lu Hui, Administrator of Shih-hsing, was appointed Governor of Kuang Province.

literal: On the ting-ssu day, Wang Fang-p'ai, Governor of Yen Province, was made Governor of Ch'ing and Chi provinces.
idiomatic: On the ting-ssu day, Wang Fang-p'ai, Governor of Yen Province, was appointed Governor of Ch'ing and Chi provinces.

literal: That year, the Prince of Wu-tu, the state of Ho-nan, Kao-li, Wa, Fu-nan, and Lin-yi all sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: That year, the Prince of Wu-tu, the state of Ho-nan, Kao-li, Wa, Fu-nan, and Lin-yi all sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the wu-yin day of the first month in spring of the sixteenth year, the imperial carriage reviewed troops at the northern suburb.
idiomatic: On the wu-yin day of the first month in spring of the sixteenth year, the Emperor reviewed troops at the northern suburb.

literal: On the keng-yin day, I-k'ang, Prince of P'eng-ch'eng, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yang Province, was advanced in rank to Grand General; he continued as Minister over the Masses, and the rest of his offices remained as before.
idiomatic: On the keng-yin day, Prince of P'eng-ch'eng I-k'ang, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yang Province, was advanced to Grand General; he remained Minister over the Masses, and his other offices were unchanged.

literal: I-chung, Prince of Chiang-hsia, General Who Campaigns North, Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Southern Yen Province, was advanced in rank to Minister of Works; his governorship remained as before.
idiomatic: Prince of Chiang-hsia I-chung, General Who Campaigns North, Commissioner with Credentials Equal to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Southern Yen Province, was advanced to Minister of Works; his governorship was unchanged.

literal: Wang Ching-hung, Special Grandee and Left Grandee of Splendid Virtue, was given the privilege of a separate office equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Wang Ching-hung, Special Grandee and Left Grandee of Splendid Virtue, received the privilege of a separate office equal to the Three Dukes.

literal: On the kuei-ssu day, Ching Province was again divided to establish Hsiang Province.
idiomatic: On the kuei-ssu day, Ching Province was again divided to establish Hsiang Province.

literal: On the chi-hai day of the second month, I-chi, Prince of Heng-yang and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Ching Province.
idiomatic: On the chi-hai day of the second month, Prince of Heng-yang I-chi, Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Ching Province.

literal: On the ting-wei day, Chün, Prince of Shih-hsing, was made Governor of Hsiang Province.
idiomatic: On the ting-wei day, Prince of Shih-hsing Chün was appointed Governor of Hsiang Province.

literal: On the kuei-hai day, the six commanderies of Pa-hsi, Tzu-t'ung, Southern Tang-ch'ü, Southern Han-chung from Liang Province and Nan-an and Huai-ning from Southern Ch'in Province were severed [20] and placed under Yi Province.
idiomatic: On the kuei-hai day, the six commanderies of Pa-hsi, Tzu-t'ung, Southern Tang-ch'ü, Southern Han-chung from Liang Province and Nan-an and Huai-ning from Southern Ch'in Province were detached [20] and assigned to Yi Province.

literal: Pa-ling Commandery was established from the commanderies of Ch'ang-sha and Chiang-hsia and placed under Hsiang Province.
idiomatic: Pa-ling Commandery was carved out of Ch'ang-sha and Chiang-hsia commanderies and placed under Hsiang Province.

literal: On the ting-ssu day of the fourth month in summer, I-hsuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Chiang Province, was made General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province.
idiomatic: On the ting-ssu day of the fourth month in summer, Prince of Nan-ch'iao I-hsuan, General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Chiang Province, was appointed General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province.

literal: I-ch'ing, Prince of Lin-ch'uan and General Who Pacifies the West, was made General of the Guard and Governor of Chiang Province.
idiomatic: Prince of Lin-ch'uan I-ch'ing, General Who Pacifies the West, was appointed General of the Guard and Governor of Chiang Province.

literal: On the chi-yu day of the sixth month, Murong Yen of Lung-hsi T'o-yü-hun was changed in enfeoffment to Prince of Ho-nan.
idiomatic: On the chi-yu day of the sixth month, Murong Yen of Lung-hsi T'o-yü-hun was redesignated Prince of Ho-nan.

literal: On the kuei-ch'ou day, Shih-pin of T'o-yü-hun was made General Who Pacifies the West, and Fan-ni of T'o-yü-hun was made General Who Pacifies the Army.
idiomatic: On the kuei-ch'ou day, Shih-pin of T'o-yü-hun was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, and Fan-ni of T'o-yü-hun was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army.

literal: On the keng-tzu day of the eighth month in autumn, the fourth imperial son Shuo was established as Prince of Nan-p'ing.
idiomatic: On the keng-tzu day of the eighth month in autumn, the fourth imperial son Shuo was created Prince of Nan-p'ing.

literal: On the i-wei day of the intercalary month, I-hsin, Prince of Ch'ang-sha, General of the Army and Governor of Yü Province, died.
idiomatic: On the i-wei day of the intercalary month, Prince of Ch'ang-sha I-hsin, General of the Army and Governor of Yü Province, died.

literal: On the wu-hsü day, Huai-nan from Yü Province was again divided to establish Southern Yü Province.
idiomatic: On the wu-hsü day, Huai-nan was again severed from Yü Province to establish Southern Yü Province.

literal: On the kuei-mao day, Liu Tsun-k'ao, General of the Left Guards, was made Governor of Yü Province.
idiomatic: On the kuei-mao day, Liu Tsun-k'ao, General of the Left Guards, was appointed Governor of Yü Province.

literal: On the wu-shên day, Chün, Prince of Shih-hsing and Governor of Hsiang Province, was made Governor of Southern Yü Province, and Chün, Prince of Wu-ling, was made Governor of Hsiang Province.
idiomatic: On the wu-shên day, Prince of Shih-hsing Chün, Governor of Hsiang Province, was appointed Governor of Southern Yü Province, and Prince of Wu-ling Chün became Governor of Hsiang Province.

literal: On the i-hai day of the twelfth month in winter, the Heir Apparent underwent the capping ceremony, and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the i-hai day of the twelfth month in winter, the Heir Apparent underwent the capping ceremony, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: That year, the Prince of Wu-tu, the Prince of Ho-nan, Lin-yi, and Kao-li sent envoys bearing tribute.
idiomatic: That year, the Prince of Wu-tu, the Prince of Ho-nan, Lin-yi, and Kao-li sent envoys bearing tribute.

literal: On the wu-wu day, the first of the fourth month in summer of the seventeenth year, there was a solar eclipse.
idiomatic: On the wu-wu day, the first of the fourth month in summer of the seventeenth year, there was a solar eclipse.

literal: On the kuei-ssu day of the fifth month, Liu Chan, General of the Army of the Palace Guard, left office on his mother's mourning.
idiomatic: On the kuei-ssu day of the fifth month, Liu Chan, General of the Army of the Palace Guard, left office to observe mourning for his mother.
